suite.title: Material cues at two rendering qualities (WebXR)

study.title: Material cues at two rendering qualities (WebXR)
study.researchQuestion: RQ1: How does the rendering quality of a WebXR room (low: flat, unlit colours; high: physically based materials) affect how quickly and accurately people find objects defined by their material, how well they identify materials, how present they feel, how visually appealing they find the room, and which quality they prefer?
study.agentQuestions: RQ2: Which agent methods (text only, general evidence, experiencing the app, reading the app's files, measured task data) reproduce the human differences between the two rendering qualities? RQ3: Does knowing each participant's background (vision correction, colour vision, art or design training, VR experience, age), with or without general evidence about observer differences, give useful individual forecasts?

conditions.label: High rendering quality (physically based materials, reflections, soft shadows)

phases.label: Questionnaire after each design; preference at the end

cases.label: Main: four search trials (select the glossy ceramic mug, the brushed-metal bowl and the glass vase), then six identification trials (name the material of the marked object)
Main: four search trials (select the glossy ceramic mug, the brushed-metal bowl and the glass vase), then six identification trials (name the material of the marked object)

sources.label: Study brief
sources.description: examples/material-cues/agent-brief.md: the room, the two rendering qualities, the tasks and the questionnaire, without any participant answers.

sources.label: WebXR project
sources.description: examples/material-cues/webxr-app/: the scene, the materials per rendering quality and the task logic. Layouts are drawn at random per session, so the code holds no layout. Run it with ?quality=low|high&study=1.

sources.label: Background: rendering and material perception
sources.description: examples/material-cues/evidence/rendering-and-material-perception.md: invented, literature-style background on material cues, visual search, presence and visual preference. Written without this study's data.

sources.label: Background: observer differences
sources.description: examples/material-cues/evidence/observer-differences.md: invented, literature-style background on how colour vision, training, VR experience, age and vision correction relate to material judgements and VR studies. Written without this study's data.

sources.label: Participant background
sources.description: data/raw/background.csv: invented background per participant; never results. Population forecasts get a cohort summary, individual forecasts the person's own row.

outcomes.label: Search time
outcomes.description: Seconds from the start of a search trial until its third target is selected (wrong selections included), geometric mean over the four search trials; practice excluded. The experimenter stops a trial at 120 s.

outcomes.label: Wrong selections
outcomes.unit: wrong selections in the four search trials
outcomes.description: Number of non-target objects selected in the four search trials together (a whole number per person and design).

outcomes.label: Material identification accuracy
outcomes.unit: proportion of six identification trials correct
outcomes.description: Share of the six identification trials (each look-alike marked once) whose material was named correctly from five options.

outcomes.label: Presence (4 items)
outcomes.description: Mean of four 1-7 presence items (general, spatial, involvement, realness), asked after each design.

outcomes.label: Visual appeal
outcomes.description: 'How visually appealing was the room?' (1-7), asked after each design.

outcomes.label: Preference
outcomes.description: At the end of the session: which of the two designs the participant preferred (rank 1) and which not (rank 2).

instructions: Predict the declared human outcomes for every design. Keep your own behaviour and time separate from the participants'. Use only supplied sources. Return every requested numeric outcome, including the named items for composites. Report uncertainty and limitations separately.

notes: Built-in deterministic analyzer using the embedded study outcomes, family weights, tie tolerance, bootstrap draws and seed.
Contrasts may be added by later continuations; they do not change the scoring definition of existing outcomes.
Each condition is one agent protocol. Continuations may add models, protocols and repetitions; unchanged jobs are reused.
